{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"HowTo","name":"How to Check if an iPhone Is Stolen","description":"Check an iPhone IMEI, Activation Lock, Find My, carrier status, parts history, and seller paperwork before buying a used iPhone.","step":[{"@type":"HowToStep","position":1,"name":"Step 1","text":"Find and photograph the item's identifier. Open Settings → General → About, or dial *#06# for the IMEI. Apple also explains where identifiers appear on supported models and packaging."},{"@type":"HowToStep","position":2,"name":"Step 2","text":"Match the identifiers: Compare Settings → General → About with the box and any identifier printed on the SIM tray. Apple has no public serial-number page that tells a buyer whether Activation Lock is enabled."},{"@type":"HowToStep","position":5,"name":"Step 5","text":"Check carrier and finance status: Use the original carrier’s official eligibility tool or contact the carrier with the IMEI. Ask about network eligibility and device-payment restrictions."},{"@type":"HowToStep","position":6,"name":"Step 6","text":"Run a SafeOrStolen IMEI check: SafeOrStolen checks its own stolen-item reports, public web results, and AI analysis, and provides IMEI device details.
